newsitem.title: CANADA: Abacan hits high ahead of Nigeria results.
newsitem.headline: Abacan hits high ahead of Nigeria results.

text.p: Shares of Abacan Resource Corp hit a new high in heavy volume on Thursday as speculation intensified over coming results from its long-awaited Aje #1 deep water oil well off the coast of Nigeria.
Canada's Abacan climbed C$0.05 in Toronto Stock Exchange trade to C$10.45 on turnover of 1.8 million shares after hitting an earlier session high of C$10.65.
"We completed the drilling phase, we have logged and now we're preparing to test and we should have test results probably late next week," said company spokesperson Lon Boshouwers.
The Aje #1 well, on Abacan's Block 309, began drilling in March but suffered several delays because of mechanical and technical glitches.
Abacan chief executive Wade Cherwayko has said the 11,000-foot-deep well had the potential to prove Block 309 oil reserves of between 200 million and 400 million barrels of oil.
Boshouwers declined to comment on the company's current preliminary expectations for the well.
Aje #1 targeted three different geological zones, the company has said.
Meanwhile, the Abacan was still on track to start production from its NGO field in Nigeria's Niger Delta in early November, Boshouwers said.
Abacan expects NGO to yield about 30,000 to 40,000 barrels of oil per day at the end of this year and production would be increased to 50,000 barrels per day in early 1997.
Abacan shares climbed to Thursday's level from C$4.78 on July 12.
